entries.name: QueueBuilder
entries.signature: export type QueueBuilder<TContext, TMeta extends QueueMeta = QueueMeta> = { /** * The configuration used to create this builder */ readonly _config: QueueConfig; /** * Base job builder with no middleware * Similar to tRPC's base procedure * Output context is JobContext<TContext> because runtime wraps user context */ readonly job: JobBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Create middleware for jobs * * By default, middleware maintains JobContext<TContext> as both input and output. * Provide explicit type parameters to transform context: * - middleware<MyContextIn, MyContextOut>(...) for full control * - middleware<MyContext>(...) to use same type for input and output */ middleware: { <TContextIn = JobContext<TContext>, TContextOut = TContextIn>(fn: MiddlewareFunction<TContextIn, TContextOut, TMeta>): JobMiddleware<TContextIn, TContextOut, TMeta>; <TContextIn = JobContext<TContext>, TContextOut = TContextIn, TFailure extends Failure = never>(fn: MiddlewareFunction<TContextIn, TContextOut, TMeta, TFailure>): JobMiddleware<TContextIn, TContextOut, TMeta, TFailure>; }; /** * Create a job registry for organizing jobs by feature */ registry: <TRegistry extends Record<string, unknown>>(jobs: TRegistry) => TRegistry; /** * Create a schedule builder */ schedule: ScheduleBuilderFactory<TContext, TMeta>; /** * Create a flow builder */ flow: FlowBuilderFactory<TContext, TMeta>; /** * Create a queue instance that can register and run jobs */ createQueue: (options: { connection: QueueConnection; keyPrefix?: string; createContext: () => TContext | Promise<TContext>; }) => BullMQQueueInstance; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Queue builder returned by initQueue Similar to tRPC's initTRPC builder

entries.name: ScheduleBuilderDef
entries.signature: export type ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta extends QueueMeta> = { /** * Add middleware to the inline schedule's handler. A schedule that wraps a * job has no middleware of its own, so the builder this returns has no `.job()`. */ use<TContextOut2>(middleware: JobMiddleware<TContextOut, TContextOut2, TMeta>): ScheduleBuilderWithMiddleware<TContext, TContextOut2, TMeta>; /** * Wrap an existing job: each tick adds `.data()` to the job's own queue. * Any built job fits: its own worker runs it, with its own middleware and context. */ job<TInput>(job: JobDefinition<TInput, unknown, never>): ScheduleJobWrapper<TInput>; /** * Name the schedule (defaults to `<job name>-schedule` for `.job()`; required for an inline handler) */ name(name: string): ScheduleBuilderNamed<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Schedule builder definition

entries.name: ScheduleBuilderFactory
entries.signature: export type ScheduleBuilderFactory<TContext, TMeta extends QueueMeta> = { /** * Create a cron-based schedule * Output context is JobContext<TContext> because runtime wraps user context */ cron(pattern: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Create an interval-based schedule (repeating) * Output context is JobContext<TContext> because runtime wraps user context */ interval(milliseconds: number): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Create a timeout-based schedule (one-time execution after delay) * Output context is JobContext<TContext> because runtime wraps user context * * @example * ```typescript * // Send reminder email once after 24 hours * const reminder = q.schedule * .timeout(24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) * .job(sendReminderJob) * .data({ userId: 'usr_123' }); * ``` */ timeout(milliseconds: number): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Every N seconds (requires 6-field cron support in BullMQ) * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.everySeconds(5).job(task).data({}) // Every 5 seconds * q.schedule.everySeconds(30).job(task).data({}) // Every 30 seconds * ``` */ everySeconds(n: number): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Every N minutes * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.everyMinutes(5).job(task).data({}) // Every 5 minutes * q.schedule.everyMinutes(15).job(task).data({}) // Every 15 minutes * ``` */ everyMinutes(n: number): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Every N hours * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.everyHours(2).job(task).data({}) // Every 2 hours * q.schedule.everyHours(6).job(task).data({}) // Every 6 hours * ``` */ everyHours(n: number): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Daily at specified time (HH:mm format) * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.daily('09:00').job(task).data({}) // Every day at 9am * q.schedule.daily('14:30', { timezone: 'America/New_York' }).job(task).data({}) // Every day at 2:30pm ET * ``` */ daily(time: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Weekdays (Monday-Friday) at specified time * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.weekdays('09:00').job(task).data({}) // Weekdays at 9am * q.schedule.weekdays('17:30').job(task).data({}) // Weekdays at 5:30pm * ``` */ weekdays(time: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Weekends (Saturday-Sunday) at specified time * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.weekends('10:00').job(task).data({}) // Weekends at 10am * q.schedule.weekends('14:00').job(task).data({}) // Weekends at 2pm * ``` */ weekends(time: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Weekly on specific day at specified time * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.weekly('monday', '09:00').job(task).data({}) // Mondays at 9am * q.schedule.weekly('friday', '17:00').job(task).data({}) // Fridays at 5pm * ``` */ weekly(day: 'monday' | 'tuesday' | 'wednesday' | 'thursday' | 'friday' | 'saturday' | 'sunday', time: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; /** * Monthly on specific day at specified time * * @example * ```typescript * q.schedule.monthly(1, '09:00').job(task).data({}) // First day of month at 9am * q.schedule.monthly(15, '12:00').job(task).data({}) // 15th of month at noon * ``` */ monthly(day: number, time: string, options?: { timezone?: string; }): ScheduleBuilderDef<TContext, JobContext<TContext>, TMeta>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Schedule builder factory

entries.name: ScheduleBuilderNamed
entries.signature: export type ScheduleBuilderNamed<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta extends QueueMeta> = { /** * Wrap an existing job under this schedule name */ job<TInput>(job: JobDefinition<TInput, unknown, never>): ScheduleJobWrapper<TInput>; /** * Set input schema (unlocks `.handler()`) */ input<TNewInput>(schema: StandardSchemaV1<unknown, TNewInput>): ScheduleBuilderChain<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta, TNewInput, never>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Schedule builder after `.name()` with no middleware: wrap a job, or set the input of an inline handler. Has no `.handler()` until `.input()` runs.

entries.name: ScheduleBuilderNeedsInput
entries.signature: export type ScheduleBuilderNeedsInput<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta extends QueueMeta> = { /** * Set input schema (unlocks `.handler()`) */ input<TNewInput>(schema: StandardSchemaV1<unknown, TNewInput>): ScheduleBuilderChain<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta, TNewInput, never>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Schedule builder after name is set, before input is set. Has no `.handler()`: calling it here is a compile error ("Call .input() first").

entries.name: ScheduleBuilderWithMiddleware
entries.signature: export type ScheduleBuilderWithMiddleware<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta extends QueueMeta> = { /** * Add more middleware to the inline schedule's handler */ use<TContextOut2>(middleware: JobMiddleware<TContextOut, TContextOut2, TMeta>): ScheduleBuilderWithMiddleware<TContext, TContextOut2, TMeta>; /** * Set name for inline handler */ name(name: string): ScheduleBuilderNeedsInput<TContext, TContextOut, TMeta>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Schedule builder after `.use()`: only an inline handler can follow. Has no `.job()`: wrapping a job here is a compile error (the job's own middleware applies).
